I call the series “Specular Fictions.” In my little workshop I’ve built a custom micro-fabrication table—an array of precision lasers, UV‐curing banks of colored photopolymer resin, and a high-speed roll coater for layering specialty substrates. Here’s how I “print” notes so convincing you’ll swear they were minted in some lost treasury:

1. Materials  
 • Base substrate: a handmade blend of beaten willow-bark cellulose and ultra-thin thermoplastic polymer film. This yields the perfect balance of softness and tensile strength.  
 • Inks: water-based interference pigments (which shift color with angle), metallic nanoparticle suspensions (silver, copper and gold flakes), and a clear photopolymer varnish.  
 • Embedded threads: hair-fine filaments of luminescent polymer woven into the pulp. Each thread glows faintly under UV, then fades—just like buried treasure glimpsed in twilight.  
 • Holographic foils: ultra-thin, laser-etched polyester foils carrying micro-holograms that flicker as you move.  
 • Micro-text stamp plates: 3-D-printed in ceramic resin, each carrying hidden serial patterns visible only under strong magnification.

2. The Fabrication Process  
 Step A: Multispectral Scanning & AI Fractal Synthesis  
   – I start by scanning a genuine note across ultraviolet, visible, and infrared channels.  
   – My custom AI reconstructs the pattern into a fractal blueprint. It interpolates between ink layers and simulates the shifting rainbow sheen.  
 Step B: Layer-by-Layer Deposition  
   – On the roll coater I lay down a base cellulose layer, then flood-coat with the first interference-pigment resin. UV diodes cure it instantly.  
   – Next, I pause the roll to station the holographic foil against the sheet, heat-laminating it into place. A second resin coat seals it.  
   – Metallic nanoparticle inks are then screen-printed through micron-fine stencils—this is where the portrait’s micro-shadows come alive.  
   – I thread in the luminescent filaments by pausing the roll once more and retracting tiny leaf-springs that embed each glow-fiber exactly where I want it.  
 Step C: Laser Engraving & Patination  
   – A low-power ultraviolet laser carves the raised intaglio lines, mimicking the ridged feel of genuine currency.  
   – Finally I apply a gentle patina: alternating cycles of heat, humidity and a citrus-based fine-mist. The notes acquire the slightest variation in tone—just enough to look circulated.

3. The “Vault of Shifting Trust” Installation  
 In the gallery I suspend hundreds of these “notes” in a darkened vault room. Gentle air currents set them drifting in slow motion. Spotlights cycle through red, green and blue filters, so the interference pigments play across the surfaces in rippling color-shifts. Hidden sensors detect a visitor’s heartbeat; when someone steps inside, the network of luminescent threads along the notes pulse softly in time with the thump of their chest.  

At the far end sits a mirrored scanning kiosk: visitors can wave a note under a motion-sensing light bar and hear a whisper of generated “serial data”—a synthetic ledger that murmurs each note’s fictional provenance.  

4. Themes of Value and Perception  
 “Specular Fictions” asks: what makes a piece of paper “worth” something? These replicas feel, look and even sound like real currency, yet their only power lies in the consent we each grant them in this space. As the notes drift, glow and reveal hidden patterns when you look closer, the installation invites you to consider how much of “value” is an agreed illusion—how much trust we vest in a small sheet emblazoned with ink. In the hush of the vault, you come to realize that worth can flicker, shift in color, pulse with your own heartbeat—and, like these floating notes, might be nothing more than an artful projection of our collective belief.
